Article Title: India-US ‘pretty close’ to signing a ‘different kind of deal,’ says Donald Trump
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump

Rubio calls India-US alignment ‘extraordinary’

US, India officials express optimism over negotiations

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday (local time) said India and the United States were “pretty close” to finalising a trade deal after more than a year of negotiations. He further added that the agreement “could be a much different kind of deal”.“They want to make a deal. We’re going to make a deal. Pretty close, yeah,” Trump told reporters at the White House when asked about the prospects of an agreement. His remarks come amid growing optimism on both sides over the long-pending deal, with US secretary of state Marco Rubio also describing it as “incredibly close” during his visit to India.Rubio and external affairs minister S Jaishankar held wide-ranging discussions in Mumbai on Tuesday, reviewing the full scope of India-US relations and committing to an early conclusion of the proposed Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA).The meeting took place against the backdrop of the US Freedom 250 Reception hosted by US ambassador to India Sergio Gor in Mumbai. The ministry of external affairs (MEA) said that the discussions covered key strategic sectors, including trade, defence, technology and energy security. "They welcomed the progress made in negotiations on the India–US Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA) and reaffirmed their commitment to working towards its early conclusion," the MEA stated.The ministry added that Rubio's visit reflected "the sustained momentum of high-level exchanges between the two countries, underscoring the importance both sides attach to further advancing the India-US COMPACT for the 21st century."Rubio is on an official visit to India from October 20 to 21 at Jaishankar's invitation. The trip marks his second visit to the country, following an earlier trip to New Delhi in May. He will next travel to Jamnagar in Gujarat for discussions that will include "enhanced energy cooperation", according to the US state department.Earlier on Tuesday, Rubio described the strategic alignment between India and the United States as “extraordinary”, saying the two countries had an opportunity to shape the course of the 21st century through their partnership.Speaking at the Freedom 250 Reception in Mumbai, he acknowledged that the two countries would not agree on every issue but said their shared interests could shape geopolitics, economics, trade and commerce for decades.“No two nations on Earth will ever be perfectly aligned on every issue, and there will be times and points of disagreement,” Rubio stated. “But on the core issues that matter, the core issues that define the national interests of both India and the United States, the alignment between our countries is extraordinary,” he added.Rubio also said the United States should engage diplomatically with India more frequently, describing the country as one of Washington's most important geopolitical partners.Explaining the significance of his Mumbai visit, Rubio highlighted the city's role as India's financial and commercial hub, with many companies investing in and trading with the United States based there.Trump's comments follow recent positive assessments from officials in both countries about the prospects of an agreement after a prolonged stalemate over trade between Washington and New Delhi.Last week, Gor told the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi that the “the big items are done” and that the two countries were very close to “landing it.”Jaishankar had also said he was “encouraged” by progress in the trade talks, adding that both sides were “heading toward a landing point.”The negotiations have also unfolded against the backdrop of Trump's decision late Friday to waive tariffs of as much as 100% on buyers of Russian oil and gas. The duties would have affected Indian products and complicated the trade discussions.Trump's latest remarks, alongside Rubio's assessment that the agreement is down to technical details, point to continued progress towards a deal. Both sides have, however, stressed that every detail must be agreed upon by both sides before the agreement is announced.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump said India and the United States were “pretty close” to finalising a trade deal. He further added that the agreement “could be a much different kind of deal” His remarks come amid growing optimism on both sides over the long-pending deal. US secretary of state Marco Rubio also described it as ‘incredibly close’ during his visit to India.

Article Title: Crude holds near $110 per barrel as Middle East tensions keep supply concerns alive
Article Text:
Brent crude hovers near $110 per barrel

Houthi attacks add to supply concerns

Oil prices hovered near $110 a barrel on Tuesday as traders assessed the impact of Washington’s decision to ease some restrictions on Russian energy exports, while fresh attacks claimed by Yemen’s Houthis against Saudi targets added to concerns over potential supply disruptions in the Middle East.WTI crude was trading at $98.72, up 18 cents, or 0.18%, while Brent crude stood at $109.70, gaining 16 cents, or 0.15%. Brent had climbed to $110.70 a barrel in the previous session, its highest level since May 20.The market was weighing the possibility of additional Russian oil and fuel supplies following an executive order issued by US President Donald Trump on Friday night. The order waived key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs, including duties on Russian goods and penalties for purchasing the country’s oil and gas. However, Trump said on Saturday that he had yet to announce a final decision, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio said officials needed more time to assess the situation.Russia’s crude oil production rose by 65,000 barrels per day in September to 8.43 million barrels per day, according to the International Energy Agency last week. Despite the increase, output remained around 870,000 barrels per day below the level recorded a year earlier.The prospect of more Russian supplies has offered a possible counterweight to concerns about disruptions elsewhere, but risks to energy infrastructure in the Gulf region remain a key concern for traders.Fresh security concerns emerged after Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said on Monday they had carried out several attacks targeting Saudi energy, airport and military facilities. The sites named included an Aramco facility in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield, King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha airport.Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the claims, and Reuters could not independently verify them.Separately, an attack by the Houthis on a government security forces training camp in Yemen’s Shabwa province on Monday killed 58 people and injured more than 200.The latest attacks have added to concerns about regional stability and the safety of energy supplies, helping keep oil prices above the $100-a-barrel mark despite the prospect of increased Russian supply.
Article Summary: WTI crude was trading at $98.72, up 18 cents, or 0.18%, while Brent crude stood at $109.70. Brent had climbed to $110.70 a barrel in the previous session, its highest level since May 20. Fresh attacks claimed by Yemen’s Houthis against Saudi targets added to concerns over potential supply disruptions.

Article Title: Retired PSU bank employee claimed Rs 9.29 lakh leave encashment as tax-free, but taxman restricted exemption to Rs 3 lakh; ITAT applies Rs 25 lakh limit retrospectively, cancels Rs 6.29 lakh addition
Article Text:
On September 22, 2026, the ITAT Jaipur ruled in the retired bank employee’s favour. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Kamal Kumar Kalia v. Union of India

Why did the retired bank employee get tax relief from ITAT?

Kamal Kumar Kalia

Dashrath Kumar Sen v. ACIT

Govind Chhatwani v. CIT (Appeals)

Leave encashment is tax-free up to a limit for non-government employees. While the limit was earlier Rs 3 lakh, it was revised to Rs 25 lakh in 2023. There is no such upper limit for government employees. What happens if you don’t know the limit and do not pay tax on your leave encashment.In one such case a retired employee of State Bank of India (SBI) got leave encashment but did not pay tax.Under income tax law, SBI staff are treated as non-government employees and, therefore, can claim leave encashment exemption subject to the applicable limit.A retired SBI employee from Jaipur, was unaware of this distinction. When he retired in 2020 he received Rs 9.29 lakh as leave encashment and did not pay tax on the amount.Also Read | Man sold his house and bought a Rs 1.10 crore flat jointly with wife; income tax department denies Rs 55.48 lakh capital gains exemption for half the amount, but ITAT Mumbai gives full relief At that time, the exemption limit was Rs 3 lakh. It was subsequently increased to Rs 25 lakh in 2023 through Notification No. S.O. 2276(E).Under the limit applicable when the man retired, he would technically have been liable to pay tax on Rs 6.29 lakh, the amount that exceeded the Rs 3 lakh exemption.The man filed his income tax return (ITR) declaring total income of Rs 6.76 lakh from pension and other sources.In the return, he claimed an exemption of the entire Rs 9.29 lakh received as leave encashment under Section 10(10AA), which covers the cash equivalent of leave salary received at retirement.When the Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) processed his return, the claim was restricted to Rs 3 lakh. The officer added the remaining Rs 6.29 lakh to Gupta's taxable income, taking his total income to Rs 13.05 lakh, according to an ET report on the judgement.The Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), or CIT(A), upheld the adjustment, relying on the Delhi High Court's judgment in[2020] 268 Taxman 398 (Delhi).The man however appealed before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Jaipur.On September 22, 2026, the ITAT Jaipur ruled in the retired bank employee’s favour.Also Read | She bought shares for Rs 13.5 lakh and sold them for Rs 77.47 lakh after 18 months; taxman denied capital gains exemption, but ITAT gives relief and deletes Rs 79 lakh in additions The Jaipur tax tribunal noted that the distinction between government employees and other employees under clause (10AA) of Section 10 had been upheld by the Delhi High Court in(supra). The High Court had ruled that employees of public sector undertakings and nationalised banks could not claim the same status as government employees for this purpose.The ITAT Jaipur observed that the revised leave encashment exemption limit of Rs 25 lakh took effect from April 1, 2023, following the notification issued on May 24, 2023.According to the tribunal, the 2023 revision did not amount to the introduction of a new exemption. Instead, it was the belated fulfilment of an obligation, as the exemption ceiling had remained at Rs 3 lakh since 2002 despite successive revisions to salaries.ITAT Jaipur observed: “A notification of that character is remedial, and to withhold its benefit from an employee who retired shortly before it was issued would perpetuate the very disparity it was meant to remove.”Also Read | Rs 5.89 crore FD interest slashed from 7.75% to 3.5% without notice; Delhi High Court rejects bank’s non-renewal argument and orders interest at an average of earlier rates The tribunal also noted that its Coordinate Benches had consistently adopted the same approach in cases involving retired bank employees. These included[2025] 172 taxmann.com 772 (Jaipur - Trib.), which dealt with the same assessment year, AY 2020-21, and[2026] 187 taxmann.com 389 (Jaipur - Trib.).The tribunal said: “The amount of Rs 9,29,033 received by him is well within the limit of Rs 25,00,000, and no other limit prescribed by the sub-clause has been applied against him.”Accordingly, the ITAT directed the Assessing Officer (AO) to allow the full exemption of Rs 9,29,033 under Section 10(10AA) and delete the addition of Rs 6,29,033.Also Read | Grandmother and her son gifted 2.5-acre land to his second wife, who sold it; his daughter from first marriage claimed it was ancestral, but Madras HC rejects her plea Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana told ET that the Jaipur Bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) extended the enhanced Rs 25 lakh exemption limit for leave encashment to a retired State Bank of India employee, even though his case concerned assessment year 2020-21, before the statutory limit was raised in 2023.Surana points out that the tribunal did not classify SBI employees as equivalent to Central or State Government employees. It made clear that staff working for public-sector undertakings and nationalised banks are not eligible for the unlimited leave encashment tax exemption available to government employees.The ITAT Jaipur held that denying the revised benefit to someone who had retired shortly before the higher limit was notified would continue the very disparity that the change was intended to address.
Article Summary: Leave encashment is tax-free up to a limit for non-government employees. The limit was earlier Rs 3 lakh, it was revised to Rs 25 lakh in 2023. A retired SBI employee from Jaipur, was unaware of this distinction. When he retired in 2020 he received Rs 9.29 lakh and did not pay tax.

Article Title: AI boom set to push Big Tech investment beyond $1 trillion in 2027, says UBS
Article Text:
Tech giants' AI spending to exceed $1 trillion in 2027

AI spending supports US economic growth

Rising investment puts pressure on cash flows

Big tech firms are set to splurge over $1 trillion on AI infrastructure in 2027 as demand for computing power continues to grow faster than supply, according to a report by UBS.The investment boom is also helping boost US economic growth, even as companies face rising funding needs. Spending on AI infrastructure is expected to cross $600 billion in 2026 before topping $1 trillion in 2027, the report stated.“Demand has exceeded capacity ahead of schedule,” UBS said, pointing to the growing pressure on companies to expand their computing infrastructure to keep up with demand.It expects spending to rise further over the next year, although the pace of growth could peak in 2027. Higher investment is putting pressure on companies’ cash flows and increasing their need for additional funding.The growing investment in AI infrastructure has become a significant contributor to the US economy. According to UBS, spending on AI infrastructure added around 0.75 percentage points to US gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the first half of 2026.Rising equity prices linked to AI companies have also boosted household wealth and consumption, providing another source of support for economic activity.However, the report found little clear evidence that AI has so far led to a substantial increase in overall productivity or widespread job displacement.Its estimated effect on the overall unemployment rate remains limited, at around 0.2 percentage points or less.The impact on employment has varied across industries. Selected high-technology sectors, including software and computer systems design, recorded a 1.4 per cent year-on-year decline in employment. In contrast, construction industries supporting data centre infrastructure saw employment grow by nearly 3 per cent.While demand for AI infrastructure continues to drive investment, UBS has flagged emerging financing pressures among major technology companies. Their cash flows have weakened as spending has increased, while demand for their bond issuances has become less robust.The report said investors expect free cash flow to return to positive territory in 2028, provided companies are able to generate sufficient revenue from AI services.The ability to convert heavy infrastructure spending into sustainable revenue will therefore remain important as the investment cycle progresses.AI demand is also contributing to higher prices in some areas, including software, digital goods and electricity, according to UBS. However, the report noted that productivity gains from AI could help reduce inflation over time.The outlook for the investment cycle will depend on whether demand for computing power continues to exceed available capacity and whether technology companies can turn their growing investments into sustainable revenue growth.
Article Summary: Spending on AI infrastructure is expected to cross $600 billion in 2026 before topping $1 trillion in 2027. Higher investment is putting pressure on companies’ cash flows and increasing their need for additional funding. Growing investment in AI infrastructure has become a significant contributor to US economy.

Article Title: SpaceX profits skyrocket to $4.4 billion as revenue jumps 161%, AI business surges 830%
Article Text:
SpaceX revenue surges 161% to $14.6 billion in Q3

Starlink adds 1.6 million subscribers in three months

Computing capacity expands as investment climbs

SpaceX's Super Intelligence business has become the biggest driver of the company's latest quarterly growth, helping Elon Musk's aerospace company report a net profit of $4.4 billion in the July-September quarter.Revenue more than doubled from a year earlier, rising 161 per cent to $14.6 billion, while spending on infrastructure also increased sharply.The company's third-quarter results showed a turnaround from the year-ago period, when SpaceX recorded a net loss of $1.1 billion on revenue of $5.6 billion. Adjusted EBITDA, which measures operating performance, rose 306 per cent to $8.8 billion from $2.2 billion.The Super Intelligence (SI) business, covering computing infrastructure, models and software applications, generated $7.6 billion in revenue during the quarter. This was an 830 per cent increase from $813 million in the corresponding period last year.SpaceX said the segment added $6.7 billion in year-on-year revenue through its solutions and infrastructure. Growth was attributed to new cloud services agreements, the acquisition of Cursor and wider adoption of Grok products by enterprise customers and consumers.Connectivity services, led by Starlink, remained another major source of revenue for SpaceX.The segment brought in $5.2 billion in the quarter, marking a 69 per cent increase from $3.1 billion a year earlier. Its operating income rose 99 per cent to $2.4 billion.Starlink's consumer subscriber base reached 13.6 million as of September 30, compared with 7.2 million a year earlier. It added 1.6 million subscribers during the quarter. Monthly average revenue per user rose to $69 from $66 in the previous quarter.Space-related activities contributed $1.8 billion in revenue, up 6 per cent year-on-year. SpaceX completed 12 customer launches during the July-September period.The company also reported that its first orbital Starship flight delivered 26 Starlink V3 satellites. The deployment added around 10 times the downlink capacity of a Falcon 9 Starlink launch.SpaceX's expansion came with a steep rise in capital spending. Capital expenditure stood at $19.6 billion in the third quarter, against $6.9 billion in the same period last year, largely due to investment in computing infrastructure.The company's computing capacity reached 1.7 gigawatts by September 30, compared with 0.6 gigawatts a year earlier, as it continued building infrastructure for its Super Intelligence business.The chief financial officer said the company intended to pursue expansion while keeping its investments and balance sheet on a disciplined footing."We are building the infrastructure of the future with discipline--focused on capital efficiency, strong returns on invested capital, and maintaining a robust, investment-grade balance sheet--while moving with the velocity to capture the opportunity in front of us," the CFO said.
Article Summary: SpaceX revenue surges 161% to $14.6 billion in Q3. Starlink adds 1.6 million subscribers in three months. Super Intelligence business adds $6.7 billion in year-on-year revenue. SpaceX completed 12 customer launches during the July- September period.

Article Title: SBI data leak: Nearly 4,000 customer records found on dark web; what we know so far
Article Text:
SBI identifies 3,897 customer records in dark web data exposure

Names, addresses and loan records: What the data contained

What the hacker group has claimed

Business operations remain unaffected

NEW DELHI: The State Bank of India (SBI) on Wednesday said that it has identified 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information (PII) in data suspected to have been exposed on the dark web. The bank has launched a detailed investigation to establish the authenticity, source and extent of the alleged exposure.In an exchange filing, the country's largest lender said it received alerts about the suspected exposure on October 16 from its Threat Intelligence Service Provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In. A preliminary analysis of approximately 3,75,000 records available on the dark web found 3,897 records containing PII.“During the preliminary analysis of approximately 375,000 records available on the dark web, 3,897 customer records containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII) were identified. The exposed information reportedly included customers’ registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and CIF identifiers, lead IDs, and metadata associated with loan/lead records and other related files,” the bank stated.SBI said it had activated its cyber incident response and containment protocols and engaged an independent cybersecurity agency empanelled by CERT-In to assess the alleged compromise and the potential risks to customers and the bank.The lender clarified that the incident had no material impact on its core business operations, financial performance or business continuity, and that its core functions continued to operate normally.The information identified in the preliminary analysis reportedly included customers' registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses and residential addresses. The records also contained branch and customer information file (CIF) identifiers, lead IDs, metadata associated with loan and lead records, and other related files.The ongoing investigation will examine whether the data is authentic and complete, determine the potential source and extent of the exposure, and assess the risks associated with the incident. SBI said appropriate remedial and preventive measures were being implemented as required.The bank's statement follows a claim by an unidentified hacker group operating under the name ‘Siriusim’ that it had obtained confidential customer information allegedly linked to SBI, including personal details, loan applications and account-opening documents.Cybersecurity monitoring account CyberPulse56 highlighted the claim in a post on social media platform X. According to the account, the group purportedly possessed around 3.8 lakh data entries in CSV format and 2,722 PDF documents associated with the lender.The alleged dataset contained customers' personal information, residential addresses, loan applications, supporting documents and other application-related records. CyberPulse56 first reported the claim on October 16, saying Siriusim had presented the material as its first disclosure of the dataset.However, the authenticity and origin of the alleged exposure remain unverified.SBI said it would continue to monitor the situation and take appropriate measures in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements. The independent cybersecurity agency's assessment is underway, with remedial and preventive measures being implemented as required."We wish to submit that this does not have any material impact on Bank’s Core business operations, financial performance or business continuity. The Bank’s core business functions continue to operate normally without disruptions. A detailed assessment is currently underway and appropriate remedial and preventive measures are being implemented as required," the lender said.The alleged exposure comes amid broader concerns over cybersecurity risks facing India's financial sector. Earlier this year, the Reserve Bank of India stepped up cybersecurity requirements for commercial banks.
Article Summary: State Bank of India identifies 3,897 customer records in dark web data exposure. Bank has launched a detailed investigation to establish the authenticity, source and extent of the alleged exposure. Alleged dataset contained customers' personal information, residential addresses, loan applications, supporting documents.

Article Title: 24 million barrels a day: Gulf oil flows surge past prewar levels despite US-Iran war
Article Text:
Oil flows from the Middle East have topped prewar levels at over 24 million barrels a day despite escalating attacks on shipping in Hormuz

How oil is moving despite the attacks

Attacks raise the cost of shipping

Iran's leverage over oil flows weakens

Persian Gulf oil exports have climbed above prewar levels despite intensifying attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, as tankers adapt to the risks with US protection and alternative routes help keep supplies moving.Oil flows from the Middle East, including shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and alternative routes, averaged more than 24 million barrels a day in the week ending October 18, exceeding the prewar average of 23.3 million barrels a day, according to ship-tracking firm Kpler.However, shipments through the Strait of Hormuz remain below their earlier levels. Preliminary estimates put average flows through the strait, including offshore transfers in the Gulf of Oman, at around 14 million barrels a day during the same period, about 82% of prewar volumes, the Wall Stree Journal reported.The recovery comes as the risks to shipping remain high. Around 30 attacks on vessels have been reported in October, accounting for about 20% of all ship attacks recorded during the war, according to Michelle Wiese Bockmann, a senior analyst at maritime intelligence firm Windward.An improvised shipping system, supported by US protection, has helped tankers continue carrying crude through the high-risk waterway.Some vessels make short trips into the Gulf to load oil before travelling through Hormuz and transferring their cargo to other ships near Oman for onward delivery.Tankers often switch off their tracking signals during parts of these journeys. American air cover provides some protection along a corridor near the Omani coast, although vessels remain vulnerable to attacks.Pipelines running across Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are also helping exporters bypass the strait. Around 40% of non-Iranian crude shipped out of the Gulf in September travelled through routes that avoided Hormuz, compared with 17% before the war, Kpler estimated.“The big picture is that the system for shipping through a dangerous Strait of Hormuz is now well-established and the risk appetite of those involved in exporting oil has risen,” said Hamad Hussain, a senior commodities economist at Capital Economics.The increased willingness to take risks is partly driven by the potential returns. Traders can earn around $20 more per barrel by reselling Iraqi oil than before the war, according to Homayoun Falakshahi, Kpler's head of crude oil analysis. That translates into an additional $40 million on a supertanker carrying a typical cargo of two million barrels.Shipowners are also offering higher payments to attract crews willing to make the dangerous crossings. One China-based ship-staffing company offered seafarers as much as $25,000 for a round trip that typically takes one or two weeks, The Wall Street Journal reported.“The volumes remain high despite rising attacks, because profits make it worth the risk,” Falakshahi said.The continued movement of oil has not made the route safe. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has used drones and missiles against vessels attempting the crossing, while small boats have also been used to target shipping.The risks were illustrated by the Tanzania-flagged supertanker "Loyalty", which entered the Persian Gulf twice in September and October to load Iraqi crude. After transferring two million barrels of oil to another tanker in the Gulf of Oman in early October, it returned to the Gulf for another cargo.On October 16, the vessel was struck by a rocket-propelled grenade fired from a small boat, maritime security company Vanguard said. The projectile damaged a freshwater tank while the tanker was carrying two million barrels of Iraqi crude, according to a crew member.The danger has pushed up the cost of transporting oil. Freight for a supertanker carrying Gulf crude to China approached a record $37.37 per barrel this week, Kpler said. War-risk insurance premiums have risen to as much as 10% of a vessel's value, from less than 3% before the conflict, according to Windward.“In April, the problem was a shortage of crude. In October, it is the cost of moving it,” said Natasha Kaneva, head of the global commodities strategy team at JPMorgan.Brent crude rose to around $108 a barrel on Tuesday, reflecting concerns that the improvement in oil flows may not last if fighting intensifies again. With global inventories thinning, any renewed disruption could leave markets with limited room to absorb a supply shock.The recovery in regional exports contrasts with the pressure on Iran's own oil trade, which has been constrained by a US maritime blockade.Tehran has sought to reassert control over Hormuz, warning that neighbouring countries should not be able to export oil if Iran cannot ship its own. But the continued movement of crude through the strait and alternative routes has weakened its ability to deter regional shipments.“Iran would have to be more aggressive to achieve the same degree of control it previously possessed over oil flows from the region,” Hussain said.That leaves the market facing two competing realities: oil exports have recovered beyond prewar levels, but the cost and danger of moving crude remain elevated. Whether the recovery can be sustained will depend on the security of shipping routes and whether the conflict escalates further.
Article Summary: Oil flows from the Middle East averaged more than 24 million barrels a day in the week ending October 18. Around 30 attacks on vessels have been reported in October, accounting for about 20% of all ship attacks recorded during the war. An improvised shipping system, supported by US protection, has helped tankers carry crude through the high-risk waterway.

Article Title: Rupee jumps to 94.50 against US dollar, hits six-week high
Article Text:
Rupee gains against US dollar

NEW DELHI: Rupee jumped nearly 0.5% against the US dollar on Wednesday, climbing to a six-week high of 94.50. The rally came as foreign currency inflows linked to the Jio IPO and gains at the Dalal Street supported the currency. At the same time, support from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) also helped rupee, although rising crude oil prices and a firm dollar restricted its advance.The currency began the session at 94.78 at the interbank foreign exchange market before strengthening to 94.62 against the American currency. This marked a 29-paise gain over its previous closing level.The move came after the rupee ended Monday's session at 94.91, down 2 paise against the dollar. The forex market was shut on Tuesday for Dussehra.The Jio IPO, which opened for public subscription on Wednesday, has brought foreign dollar inflows into focus. Despite the support from these inflows, oil prices remained a concern for the rupee. Makda said elevated crude prices continued to act as a significant headwind for the domestic currency.According to Aamir Makda, commodity & currency analyst, commodity technical research at Choice Broking, "Over the course of today's session, the rupee is expected to consolidate within a trading band of 94.00 to 94.75 against the dollar.”The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against a basket of six currencies, edged up 0.06 per cent to 101.58. Brent crude futures, meanwhile, climbed 1.42 per cent to $110.33 per barrel.On the domestic front, equity markets recorded gains in early trade. BSE Sensex jumped 800 points while NSE Nifty50 advanced beyond the 23,100 levels.Foreign institutional investors (FIIs), however, continued to weigh on market sentiment through their equity sales. Exchange data showed that FIIs were net sellers to the tune of Rs 1,148.64 crore on Monday.
Article Summary: Rupee jumped nearly 0.5% against the US dollar on Wednesday, climbing to a six- week high of 94.50. The rally came as foreign currency inflows linked to the Jio IPO and gains at the Dalal Street supported the currency. But rising crude oil prices and a firm dollar restricted its advance.

Article Title: Reliance Industries stock surges 2% as Jio IPO gets fully subscribed in 100 minutes
Article Text:
On the BSE, RIL shares were trading 1.83 per cent higher at Rs 1,224.85 apiece.

Jio IPO impact

Jio IPO impact: Shares of Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance Industries (RIL) rose around 2% on Wednesday after its digital subsidiary, Jio Platforms, saw its Rs 30,213-crore initial public offering (IPO) fully subscribed within just 100 minutes of opening. The pace set a record for the quickest full subscription of a public issue.On the National Stock Exchange, RIL shares advanced as much as 1.96 per cent to Rs 1,225.60 apiece. During intraday trading, the stock had climbed 2.68 per cent to touch a high of Rs 1,234.30.On the BSE, RIL shares were trading 1.83 per cent higher at Rs 1,224.85 apiece. The stock had risen 2.64 per cent during the session to reach an intraday peak of Rs 1,234.60.Also Read | Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening Jio Platforms' Rs 30,213-crore IPO has been priced in the range of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share. Once completed, it is expected to become India's largest public issue, overtaking Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,870-crore IPO launched in 2024.The issue will remain open until October 23. At the upper end of the price band, Jio Platforms' valuation works out to approximately $108 billion.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know Demand from investors was strong from the outset. The portion set aside for Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIBs) was fully subscribed within the first 10 minutes and had attracted bids for nearly twice the allocated shares in less than half an hour.The QIB category eventually received subscriptions amounting to 2.86 times the shares on offer. Article Summary: RIL shares rose around 2% on Wednesday after its digital subsidiary, Jio Platforms, saw its Rs 30,213-crore initial public offering (IPO) fully subscribed. Article Title: SBI confirms data leak, appoints cybersecurity agency to conduct assessment
Article Text:
SBI confirms data leak

MUMBAI: The State Bank of India (SBI) has confirmed a data exposure involving customer information, identifying 3,897 records containing personally identifiable information (PII) in a preliminary analysis of around 375,000 records found on the dark web. The bank said it had activated its cyber incident response protocols and commissioned an independent cybersecurity agency to investigate the incident after receiving alerts from its threat intelligence service provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In on Oct 16.The disclosure follows a claim by cybersecurity monitoring account CyberPulse that a threat actor using the name Siriusim had leaked documents and personal data allegedly linked to SBI. The post claimed the dataset contained 375,000 rows in CSV files and 2,722 PDF documents, including customer information, loan applications, supporting documents, account-opening forms and addresses. The authenticity and full extent of the alleged exposure had not been independently verified in the post.In its notice to stock exchanges, SBI said the preliminary analysis had identified records containing customers' registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and customer information file (CIF) identifiers, lead IDs and metadata associated with loan and lead records and related files.A CIF identifier is a unique number banks use to maintain a customer's consolidated relationship and account information. Lead IDs typically identify prospective customers or applications in a bank's sales and lending processes.The bank said a detailed investigation was needed to establish the authenticity and completeness of the exposed data, determine its source and extent, and assess the risks to customers and the bank. It has engaged a cybersecurity agency empanelled by CERT-In, India's national cyber incident response agency, to conduct an independent assessment.SBI said the incident had no material impact on its core business operations, financial performance or business continuity, adding that its core functions continued to operate normally. It said the assessment was underway and remedial and preventive measures were being implemented.A threat actor is an individual or group that carries out, or claims to carry out, a cyberattack or other malicious activity. The term does not by itself establish who is responsible or whether a claim of a breach is genuine. The dark web refers to parts of the internet that are not accessible through standard search engines and typically require specialised software or configurations to access. It is sometimes used to trade stolen information, although the appearance of data there does not, by itself, establish how it was obtained.PII refers to information that can identify a person, either directly or when combined with other details. Names, phone numbers, dates of birth and residential addresses can be used for identity theft, targeted phishing and other forms of fraud if exposed. Metadata associated with loan applications may also reveal information about a customer's dealings with a bank.
Article Summary: The State Bank of India has confirmed a data exposure involving customer information. The bank identified 3,897 records containing personally identifiable information (PII) The bank said it had activated its cyber incident response protocols and commissioned an independent cybersecurity agency to investigate the incident.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: Woman claims Rs 14.70 lakh Section 54F tax exemption for flat; taxman denies saying she has many properties, but ITAT gives relief as one was company-owned and another jointly owned with husband
Article Text:
The assessment proceedings referred to three properties in Nagpur. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did ITAT rule in favour of the home owner?

Significance of ruling

You own a house and claim exemption under Section 54F of the Income Tax Act. However, the exemption is denied because the Income Tax Department believes you own more than one property.In one such case, the dispute arose because the income tax department considered that the woman owned more than one house property, making her ineligible for the deduction.However, in its order pronounced on September 10, 2026, the tribunal allowed her appeal and reversed the decision of the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals).Also Read | Cook working in a 5-star hotel gets Rs 4 crore tax notice with penalty for alleged Rs 24.62 crore sales, but he claims PAN was misused which led to wrong Form 26AS entry; why Delhi HC gave relief The Income Tax Department reopened a woman’s assessment for assessment year 2015-16, alleging that she had wrongly claimed a Rs 14.70 lakh deduction under Section 54F of the Income Tax Act.The Assessing Officer denied the deduction on the ground that she owned more than one residential house apart from the new asset, and assessed her income at Rs 16,70,500.The woman challenged the assessment before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), National Faceless Appeal Centre, but her appeal was dismissed on August 20, 2025.The assessment proceedings referred to three properties in Nagpur. The question before the tribunal was whether the ownership of the other properties meant she failed to meet the conditions for claiming the benefit.The tribunal described the dispute as follows: “The sole grievance of the assessee is against the deduction u/s.54F of the Act by the Revenue authorities alleging that assessee owned more than one house property making the assessee disentitled for claiming deduction u/s.54F of the Act.”Also Read | Husband and wife sell property; Income Tax dept alleges Rs 3.30 crore sale against Rs 1.60 crore in deed, cites WhatsApp chats, Excel sheets to claim Rs 1.70 crore cash receipts, but ITAT gives relief The tribunal examined three properties mentioned in the assessment proceedings and found that one belonged to a company in which the woman was a director, while another was jointly owned by her and her husband.It held that the company's property could not be treated as her personally owned property merely because of her association with the company.The flat was jointly owned by the woman and her husband, although she had not contributed towards its purchase.The order records: “So far as the third property, the same is jointly owned by the assessee and her husband and the assessee has not provided any amount towards the purchase of the said property.”The tribunal concluded that the woman fulfilled the conditions for claiming the deduction, stating: “The assessee has fulfilled the necessary conditions for claiming deduction u/s.54F of the Act and therefore entitled to deduction u/s.54F of the Act at Rs 14,70,000/-.”Also Read | Woman applied for 130 IPO shares, bank entered only 65; consumer commission awards Rs 37,000 for deficient service but rejects her Rs 40 lakh compensation claim The order identifies one house property owned by the woman for the purpose of its conclusion.The tribunal reversed the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals)’s finding, stating: “Finding of ld.CIT(A) is reversed.” It allowed the woman’s grounds of appeal and concluded: “In the result, the appeal of the assessee is allowed.”The tribunal thus granted the Rs 14.70 lakh deduction after examining the specific property-ownership facts before it.Kuldip Kumar, Partner at Mainstay Tax Advisors LLP notes that owning more than one residential house is one of the most common grounds on which tax authorities deny exemption under Section 54F of the Income-tax Act, 1961.In this case, the tax authorities considered three properties while denying the exemption. The ITAT observed that one property was owned by a company in which the taxpayer was a director and, therefore, could not be treated as her property merely because of her directorship.The second property was the new house acquired for claiming the Section 54F exemption and was consequently excluded from the count.The third property was jointly owned by the taxpayer and her husband. Although the taxpayer had not contributed towards its purchase, the Tribunal treated her as a joint owner of that property.The Tribunal concluded that the taxpayer owned only one residential house other than the new asset and, therefore, fulfilled the relevant ownership condition for claiming the exemption under Section 54F.“There have been several favourable judicial decisions in which appellate authorities have held that fractional or joint ownership of residential properties should not necessarily be equated with exclusive ownership for determining eligibility under Section 54F,” he tells TOI.In some cases, taxpayers have been allowed to claim the exemption despite holding fractional interests in multiple residential properties.Also Read | He inherited land from mother, redeveloped home & received Rs 75 lakh from builder; taxman denied capital gains exemption, but ITAT Delhi gives relief, ruling multiple floors can qualify as one house According to Kuldip Kumar, this ITAT ruling highlights the importance of examining the facts and ownership of each property before determining eligibility for the exemption.“Joint ownership of residential property, particularly between spouses, is common. It may arise from inheritance, estate planning, the desire to avoid future family disputes or the need to ensure that the surviving spouse can manage the property without unnecessary complications,” he adds.“For taxpayers claiming exemption under Section 86 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (corresponding to Section 54F of the Income-tax Act, 1961), these favourable judicial precedents may provide support where jointly owned properties are involved. However, the outcome will depend on the facts of each case and the judicial precedents applicable to it, and the possibility of the tax authorities taking a contrary view cannot be ruled out,” Kumar tells TOI.“A legislative clarification specifying how jointly owned or fractional interests in residential properties should be counted for the purposes of this provision would provide greater certainty, reduce litigation and benefit taxpayers at large,” he adds.Also Read | Woman declared Rs 67.4 lakh ancestral jewellery in her ITR which led to additions by tax department; ITAT Mumbai deleted it on basis of old records, but rejected her Rs 12 lakh HUF brokerage claim
Article Summary: In one such case, the dispute arose because the income tax department considered that the woman owned more than one house property. The Income Tax Department reopened a woman’s assessment for assessment year 2015-16, alleging that she had wrongly claimed a Rs 14.70 lakh deduction. The tribunal examined three properties mentioned in the assessment proceedings and found that one belonged to a company in which the woman was a director.

Article Title: GCCs emerging top career choice for tech talent: Survey
Article Text:
The gap is also visible in employees’ current workplaces. (Generative image)

BENGALURU: Indian technology professionals are increasingly looking for employers that offer hands-on artificial intelligence (AI) experience and clearly defined career paths, while multinational global capability centres (GCCs) are emerging as the preferred next career move for many, according to a Talent500 survey. Talent500 is part of ANSR, which has set up more than 200 GCCs in India.Thesurvey of 2,000 technology, product and data professionals found that 71% wanted hands-on AI upskilling, but only 29% said their employers provided it. Career growth was another major concern: 87% said clearly defined career paths were very important when evaluating an employer, while 79% said they would abandon an application or decline an offer if growth opportunities were unclear.The gap is also visible in employees’ current workplaces. Only 46% of respondents described their career paths as very clear. Among GCC employees, the figure fell to 36%, compared with 50% in IT services and 51% in startups. This could make career clarity a differentiator for GCCs competing for experienced technology talent, particularly as candidates increasingly seek clarity on career progression before joining an employer.GCCs were the first choice for the next career move for 69% of respondents, ahead of Indian product companies at 37% and IT services and outsourcing firms at 28%. Career growth was the leading factor in evaluating a GCC, cited by 48%, followed by the global parent brand at 41%, India-centre leadership and culture at 36%, and exposure to AI and technology at 33%. Vikram Ahuja, co-founder of ANSR and CEO of 1Wrk, said GCC hiring was growing 15-18% annually, with roles changing rather than hiring coming to a halt.
Article Summary: Indian technology professionals are increasingly looking for employers that offer hands-on artificial intelligence (AI) experience. Multinational global capability centres (GCCs) are emerging as the preferred next career move for many, according to a Talent500 survey. The survey of 2,000 technology, product and data professionals found that 71% wanted Hands-on AI upskilling.

Article Title: Classrooms to customers: What student founders need
Article Text:
A postgraduate timetable runs from noon to 8 pm, fitting study blocks around time for building businesses (Generative image)

Incubators also give young companies access to equipment they could not afford themselves,

BENGALURU: Classrooms have been carved out of office space inside a WeWork building on Bannerghatta Road in Bengaluru. A postgraduate timetable runs from noon to 8 pm, fitting study blocks around time for building businesses. Shrey Doshi (25), a postgraduate alumnus, walks in with a blue drink. “That’s my product. Try it,” he says, before explaining the blue spirulina and tender coconut.This is Mesa School of Business, where students must build businesses and find paying customers. Elsewhere, engineering clubs and laboratories offer another route into entrepreneurship. Across campuses, the support founders need ranges from time away from classes to equipment, early funding and introductions to buyers.“The clearest difference comes from two things: time to build and access to infrastructure,” said Richa Bajpai of Campus Fund, which invests in student-led businesses. She cited BITS Pilani’s attendance flexibility and option to take time off to build as reasons it remained among the leading institutions supplying pitches to her fund. “Students who start companies still face rigid exam schedules and attendance rules that force a choice between their degree and their company,” she said.Colleges also need to let students learn across disciplines, she added. For technical businesses, support can be tangible. IIT Jammu gave MachFly Aerospace labs, resources and early financial support to build its first prototype, Bajpai said. Incubators also give young companies access to equipment they could not afford themselves, professors with domain expertise and alumni with industry experience, she said.Bajpai points to govt grants, competitions and cloud credits as starting points for founders without family money or business connections. She also cited Human Biogenesis, whose founders came from humble backgrounds and started at BioNEST, IIT Guwahati’s incubator.The company has since completed clinical trials, raised aseed round and is moving into production, she said. At IIT Madras, director V Kamakoti described Centre for Innovation as “run by the student for the student”. Design clubs can feed into prototype development, with incubators, faculty and alumni supporting student teams. Citing Ather Energy’s journey, he spoke of “12 to 13 years of gestation” and the need for patient capital.Other businesses can test demand sooner. Campus Fundbacked Mumbai Pav Co began with Mesa classmates Tanay Agarwal and Jash Arora making food in another operator’s kitchen and selling to business customers before opening a store, Agarwal said. He already knew his family’s restaurant businesses; Arora brought culinary training. Access is uneven. Mesa’s advertised four-year undergraduate programme costs Rs 48 lakh, excluding accommodation and overseas immersions. It does not award a university degree.
Article Summary: Across campuses, the support founders need ranges from time away from classes to equipment, early funding and introductions to buyers. Incubators also give young companies access to equipment they could not afford themselves. At IIT Madras, director V Kamakoti described Centre for Innovation as ‘run by the student for the student’

Article Title: Nepal bans Priyagold biscuit after FSSAI finds serious hygiene deficiencies
Article Text:
Representational image

Nepal has barred the import, sale and distribution of Priyagold biscuits made by India based Surya Food and Agro Ltd, after food safety concerns flagged by Indian authorities.Nepal’s Food Technology and Quality Control Department (FTQCD) announced the restrictions in a notice issued on Monday, classifying the biscuits as sub-standard. The move follows action by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), which has suspended the manufacturer's licence and initiated legal proceedings for prosecution.According to FSSAI, an inspection of Surya Food and Agro revealed serious deficiencies in food safety and hygiene. The regulator also initiated prosecution proceedings against the company for using cattle feed bran in the manufacture of Priyagold biscuits, along with other serious violations.Citing FSSAI’s notice, Nepal's food department decided to prohibit the biscuits from entering or being sold in the country. The decision was taken during an emergency meeting held virtually at the initiative of department director general Sanjeev Kumar Karna.The department said that the restrictions were imposed with human health security and consumer welfare in mind.Following the ban, the FTQCD has asked relevant bodies, traders and consumers to refrain from importing Priyagold biscuits and ensure that their sale and distribution are stopped.It has also directed authorised importers and food traders to immediately recall any stocks of the biscuits that may still be available in the market.
Article Summary: Nepal has barred the import, sale and distribution of Priyagold biscuits made by India based Surya Food and Agro Ltd. The move follows action by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), which has suspended the manufacturer's licence and initiated legal proceedings for prosecution.

Article Title: Oil prices today: Brent crude tops $110 as Middle East tensions threaten shipments
Article Text:
Oil prices climb over 1% (representative image)

Tanker attacks raise concerns over oil supplies

Oil prices retreat from five-month high

US works to increase fuel supplies

Oil prices rose on Wednesday as traders weighed concerns over Middle East supplies amid growing risks to shipping in the Red Sea and threats to oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.Brent crude futures climbed $1.34, or 1.23 per cent, to $110.10 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose $1.18, or 1.21 per cent, to $99 per barrel.The gains followed a decline in the previous session, when prices eased after Iran's president discussed mediation efforts with Pakistan's army chief during a meeting in Tehran.Supply concerns intensified after a supertanker caught fire after striking a sea mine south of the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy.Iranian media reported that the vessel had been “violating” Iranian regulations.At least 18 vessel attacks were reported over a two-week period, ship-tracking firm Kpler said in a note on Monday.The attacks have also spread beyond the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil shipments.“Attacks on tankers have expanded beyond the Strait of Hormuz,” LSEG analysts said in a note.“Iran has been targeting vessels as far south as the Gulf of Oman, threatening loadings outside of the Arab Gulf, as well as the ship-to-ship transfers that have helped to support Middle East loadings as the conflict has dragged on,” the analysts added.The Houthis on Monday claimed responsibility for attacks on a Saudi Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield and the airports in Riyadh and Abha, Saudi Arabia.Meanwhile, the death toll from a Houthi attack on Yemeni government forces on Monday rose to 73 as fighting intensified, Reuters reported.Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araqchi said in a television interview aired on Tuesday that Tehran had not received a response from Saudi Arabia or Yemen's Houthis to its offer to help broker peace talks.Despite Wednesday's gains, crude prices had fallen in the previous session after reaching elevated levels.Brent crude futures settled down 76 cents, or 0.69 per cent, at $108.79 per barrel on Tuesday, after touching a five-month high of $111.99.The November contract for US WTI crude, which expired on Tuesday, settled $1.87 lower, down 1.8 per cent, at $101.79 per barrel.In the United States, two Energy Department officials said on Tuesday that they were working with refiners around the world to increase fuel production as a diesel shortage pushed prices higher.US crude oil inventories were also expected to have declined in the week ended October 16, alongside stocks of refined petroleum products, according to an extended Reuters poll.The eight analysts surveyed by Reuters estimated that US crude inventories fell by an average of around 800,000 barrels during the week.Market participants are monitoring developments across the Middle East, including threats to shipping routes and energy infrastructure, for their potential impact on oil supplies and prices.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures climbed $1.34, or 1.23 per cent, to $110.10 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 1.21 per cent to $99 per barrel. The gains followed a decline in the previous session, when prices eased after Iran's president discussed mediation efforts with Pakistan's army chief.

Article Text:
Since March, countries have recalibrated their energy purchases due to the disruption in West Asia.

European Union Sees Slowest Pace Of Increase In April-Aug

NEW DELHI: It all boils down to one commodity: Oil products. Asean has emerged as the fastest growing region for India’s exports due to a spurt in petro product shipments – mainly to Singapore -- while the European Union saw the slowest pace of increase during AprilAug as export of petroleum products fell.Latest data available with the commerce department showed that India’s exports to Asean went up 56% during the first five months of the fiscal year as oil product shipments soared 2.4 times to over $6.1 billion, with Singapore accounting for almost threefourths of it. What also helped was a 20-fold jump in computer hardware to $1.4 billion to Asean countries and strong growth of electric machinery (82% to $1.6 billion) and buffalo meat (42% to $1 billion)Since March, countries have recalibrated their energy purchases due to the disruption in West Asia.In contrast, when it comes to EU, oil product exports fell 21% to $4.6 billion as the Netherlands cut back on purchases from India. While the Netherlands was the top destination for Indian fuel, with exports of $5.3 billion during April-Aug 2025, it has now slipped to the third place, behind Singapore and Tanzania, as the value of shipments crashed 47% to $2.8 billion.A part of the impact in EU was offset by Spain and Italy. In April-Aug, India’s exports to Spain rose 54% to $3.5 billion, with oil products jumping to $1.1 billion during the period, as against $172 million ayear ago – an over six-fold increase.In case of Italy, the jump was even more dramatic as petroleum product exports rose from $4 million during April-Aug 2025 to $659 million so far this year.Oil exports to North America fell 7% to $1.9 billion and the 8% rise in overall exports to the region, largely the US, was led by iPhones as telecom instruments rose 29% to over $11 billion, accounting for 23.5% of the exports to the region. Pharma exports too fell 5% to just under $4 billion.Exports to the region slowed as the value of shipments to the US was up just over 6% to $42.8 billion, data showed.
Article Summary: Indian exports to Asean went up 56% during the first five months of the fiscal year. Oil product shipments soared 2.4 times to over $6.1 billion, with Singapore accounting for almost threefourths of it. In contrast, when it comes to EU, oil product exports fell 21% to $4.6 billion.

Article Title: Wall Street climbs as healthcare stocks hit record, oil prices ease; Dow Jones up 0.97%, S&P gains 0.42%
Article Text:
Healthcare stocks were among the biggest gainers

Wall Street's main indexes traded higher on Tuesday, with healthcare stocks reaching a record high and easing oil prices supporting sentiment as investors assessed corporate earnings and lingering concerns over artificial intelligence spending.The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.97% to 52,468.06, while the S&P 500 gained 0.42% to 7,723.06. The Nasdaq Composite edged up 0.22% to 26,489.60 as of 12.06 pm ET.Healthcare stocks were among the biggest gainers, with Eli Lilly rising 4.7 per cent to a record high. Amgen, Pfizer, Johnson & Johnson and AbbVie each advanced more than 2 per cent. Financial stocks also climbed 1.2 per cent, helping lift the broader market.Oil prices moved lower after an unsettled session in which Brent crude touched a five-month high. Brent futures fell 1.1 per cent as traders assessed reports of attacks on Saudi infrastructure by Yemen's Houthis and vessel attacks in the Gulf. Lower crude prices offered some relief amid concerns over inflation and energy supply disruptions.The gains followed a rebound on Monday, when investors returned to technology stocks after last week's sharp selloff.Concerns over the borrowing costs and debt exposure associated with the artificial intelligence boom have kept markets volatile. CoreWeave shares rose 2.5 per cent on Tuesday, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index advanced 0.7 per cent.Corporate earnings also drove individual stocks. Credit reporting firm Equifax surged 11.4 per cent after posting better-than-expected third-quarter profits, while toy maker Hasbro gained 5.6 per cent after raising its full-year revenue and digital gaming forecasts.Industrial conglomerate 3M rose 5 per cent after expanding its data-centre partnership with Amazon and increasing its annual profit outlook. General Motors dropped 6.9 per cent, however, after warning of pressure from higher commodity costs and weaker truck sales in the coming months. Steel Dynamics fell 1.4 per cent after missing quarterly profit estimates.Investors are looking to a busy earnings calendar for signs that corporate growth can withstand economic uncertainty and the high cost of financing technology investments. Netflix and SpaceX were scheduled to report results after Tuesday's market close, followed by Meta Platforms and Tesla on Wednesday.In Asia, South Korean artificial intelligence infrastructure company Elice Group fell nearly 30% on its stock market debut, trading below its initial public offering price.Market breadth remained positive, with advancing stocks outnumbering decliners by 2.51 to 1 on the New York Stock Exchange and 2.78 to 1 on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 recorded 21 new 52-week highs and one new low, while the Nasdaq Composite posted 32 new highs and 204 new lows.
Article Summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.97% to 52,468.06, while the S&P 500 gained 0.42% to 7,723.06. The Nasdaq Composite edged up 0.22% to 26,489.60 as of 12.06 pm ET. Healthcare stocks were among the biggest gainers, with Eli Lilly rising 4.7% to a record high.

Article Title: No job, but still a 9-to-5 routine: Why China's unemployed are pretending to go to work every day
Article Text:
China's unemployed are pretending to go to work every day, here's why

Nowhere to report, everywhere to go

A train to … ?

And the pretence gets harder

Keeping up appearances to keep the peace

Tired of relatives asking, “So, where are you working now?” Some young Chinese adults have found an unusual way to dodge the question — getting dressed, leaving home on time and heading out for the day.But there is one catch: they have no workplace to report to. Instead, they spend their days in libraries, parks, cafes or shopping malls, all while keeping their unemployment under wraps.Their workplace may be make-believe, but the pressure to look employed is very real.For 32-year-old Coco Li, even a photograph of lunch nearly gave away the truth. A former employee of a Chinese state-owned property firm told Reuters that she was about to post a picture of a home-cooked meal in her family group chat when she stopped herself.Sharing it could invite an obvious question from her mother: why was she at home instead of work?Li had quit her job more than six months earlier, citing a heavy workload and little recognition. But telling her family about her unemployment was not something she wanted to do. Like many others facing a difficult job market, she chose to keep up the appearance of being employed, partly to avoid the worry and pressure that would follow an admission that she was out of work."She would fall into an endless cycle of anxiety and eventually pass that anxiety on to me," Li said of her mother. Her concern, she added, "couldn't really solve my problem," she further told Reuters.Li's experience is part of a trend that has gained considerable attention on Chinese social media. People are sharing advice on how to fill working hours without a job, avoid questions from relatives and maintain the appearance of having somewhere to be every morning.The scale of the conversation is striking. Posts about pretend-workers and their daily routines have attracted more than 70 million views on RedNote, an Instagram-like app, and 610 million views on Douyin, China's TikTok. Related hashtags on Weibo, which is similar to X, have received up to 320 million views.Behind the online discussions lies a labour market in which securing employment has become increasingly difficult. Analysts see the trend as a reflection of the pressures facing workers in an economy increasingly dependent on strong exports.Monday's third-quarter data showed manufacturers grappling with fierce competition by cutting prices and reducing payrolls, while expecting the employees who remain to shoulder heavier workloads.The strain is not limited to manufacturing. China's prolonged property market crisis and tight local government finances have affected jobs and incomes, while automation and the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence have added to employment pressures.For those pretending to have jobs, the challenge is not just concealing unemployment but also finding somewhere to spend the day.Social media posts describe people moving between parks, libraries, cafes and shopping malls, keeping themselves occupied until it is time to return home. The routines recall those of salarymen in South Korea and Japan who concealed their joblessness during the Asian financial crisis of the 1990s.Li follows a similar routine when her parents come to visit.The crowds in places that might otherwise seem quiet on a weekday have also caught the attention of people experiencing the same predicament. Zhang, a 36-year-old visual effects producer who lost her job in AI-driven redundancies in August, gave only her surname."I never would have believed the library would be completely full on a weekday," she said.Online, the stories range from practical guides to personal accounts of unemployment. Some users wonder whether strangers around them are also pretending to be at work. Others explain why they have chosen to hide their circumstances and describe the emotional toll of keeping up the act.One post, titled "Day 30 of unemployment: a month pretending to work," documents a month of joblessness alongside 80 unsuccessful job applications.For Susan Sun, 28, keeping her unemployment private has become a daily exercise in managing time and appearances.Sun has concealed her layoff from an internet company since late last year. The arrangement became more difficult in May, when her mother and stepfather moved from their smaller hometown to live with her in the megacity of Chongqing as they looked for work.With her parents at home, Sun has to leave before 9 am and return after 6 pm, maintaining the rhythm of a working day even though she no longer has a job.She gets by on monthly unemployment benefits of 1,864 yuan ($278) and the remaining money from her severance package. Sun says she is content to live on little and not work. The pressure comes instead from her parents and their concerns about her finances."They pass their anxiety on to me, through subtle, insistent expressions and tone of voice," she said.The concern becomes particularly apparent when they urge her to save money because "the economy is bad."For Sun, therefore, the difficulty is not simply finding a way to occupy her time. It is also avoiding conversations that turn her financial circumstances into a source of anxiety within the family.The decision to hide unemployment can have consequences beyond individual households. Diana Fu, an associate professor of Chinese politics at Cornell University, said pretending to go to work gives people a way to save face and could also help defuse collective discontent.She said the practice helps preserve social stability as Beijing presses ahead with automation and its technological competition with the US."Pretend-workers are helping the Chinese government to stave off the hard choice between leaping ahead in automation and protecting job security, which is so essential to the social contract," she said.For those involved, however, the arrangement is also a way of managing the expectations of family members at a time when work is becoming harder to find.The pretence may offer temporary relief from difficult questions, but maintaining it requires time, effort and money — resources that can become increasingly scarce during unemployment.Financial pressure could eventually make it harder for unemployed people to continue concealing their circumstances. Yige Dong, an assistant professor of sociology at the University at Buffalo, said that China's social safety net is relatively thin compared with the support systems available in Japan and South Korea during the 1990s.
Article Summary: Some young Chinese adults have found an unusual way to dodge the question. They spend their days in libraries, parks, cafes or shopping malls, all while keeping their unemployment under wraps. Analysts see the trend as a reflection of the pressures facing workers in an economy increasingly dependent on strong exports.

Article Title: Beyond the Strait: Gulf looks for an escape route from Hormuz
Article Text:
Vessels at the Strait of Hormuz (representational image)

$1.4 trillion infrastructure pipeline

Gulf remains attractive to investors despite war

The Middle East conflict has put the world’s energy lifeline, the Strait of Hormuz, in a chokehold.But the Gulf might be looking for an escape route.Over the next five years, countries in the region could invest in alternative logistics corridors and energy pipelines to loosen their dependence on the strategic waterway and keep oil and gas flowing, HSBC group chief executive Georges Elhedery said on Tuesday.The conflict has exposed the risks of depending on the strategic waterway, which previously carried a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas trade. Gulf nations are now being pushed to direct resources towards developing energy pipelines connecting production centres to ports, potentially allowing shipments to bypass the strait.Speaking at the HSBC Future Forum in Dubai, Elhedery said the region would be able to recover from the conflict and continue growing, but that doing so would require substantial investment."We do see this region being able to recover and then continue growing. It will mean a lot of investment," the bank CEO said."Of course, we do wish and hope to see a resolution to the conflict ... But Hormuz, probably in five years' time, may become redundant," he added.The shift towards alternative routes comes as the Middle East, North Africa and Turkey have a substantial pipeline of infrastructure projects that could attract investment.According to an HSBC report published on Monday, citing data from Dubai-based construction industry market intelligence platform MEED, the regions are offering $872 billion in individual project packages. These form part of a wider $1.4 trillion pipeline of infrastructure projects that have been planned but not yet awarded.The investment pipeline comes as Gulf countries consider ways to limit the disruption caused by the conflict and strengthen their ability to move energy supplies through routes other than the Strait of Hormuz.Despite the conflict, business leaders and institutional investors continue to view the Gulf as an attractive destination for investment.A recent HSBC survey of more than 1,600 business leaders and around 820 global institutional investors found that respondents still considered the region an appealing investment hub.However, the economic outlook for the wider region has weakened. After recording growth of 3.3% in 2025, the Middle East, North Africa and Pakistan region is expected to contract by 1.3% this year because of the war, according to a World Bank forecast issued last week.The contraction is expected to be followed by a strong but uneven recovery in 2027.Elhedery was among the global financiers expected to attend Saudi Arabia's flagship investment conference next week. The event was postponed until 2027 on Monday following deadly strikes in Riyadh by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis.
Article Summary: Gulf countries could invest in alternative logistics corridors and energy pipelines to loosen their dependence on the strategic waterway. The shift towards alternative routes comes as the Middle East, North Africa and Turkey have a substantial pipeline of infrastructure projects. Despite the conflict, business leaders and institutional investors continue to view the Gulf as an attractive destination for investment.
